title: Adult tooth knocked out (dental avulsion)
summary: An adult permanent tooth knocked completely out can sometimes be re-implanted if you act within an hour. Baby teeth are NOT re-implanted.
steps: Find the tooth. Pick it up by the crown (the white part) — never touch the root.
If the tooth is dirty, rinse it gently with cool clean water or milk for no more than 10 seconds. Do not scrub it.
If you can, place the tooth back in its socket the right way around and have the person bite gently on a clean cloth to hold it in place.
If you cannot re-implant it, store the tooth in milk, or in saliva (in the cheek for an adult who is alert and not at risk of choking). Plain water is a last resort.
Control any bleeding from the empty socket by biting on a clean folded cloth for 10–15 minutes.
Get the person to a dentist or emergency dental service as fast as possible, ideally within 30–60 minutes.
avoid: Do not touch or scrub the root of the tooth.
Do not store the tooth in plain water for long — it damages the root cells.
Do not try to re-implant a baby tooth — it can damage the developing adult tooth underneath.
Do not delay seeing a dentist — survival of the tooth drops fast after an hour.
whenToEscalate: Always — a dentist or emergency dental service should see the person within the hour for the best chance of saving the tooth.
An emergency department visit is needed if there is a serious facial injury, suspected jaw fracture, or heavy bleeding that will not stop with pressure.
specialty: Emergency dentist; emergency department for associated facial trauma.

sources.title: International Association of Dental Traumatology — avulsion guidelines
